title: promotion-guardrails asserts containment and reports fast-forwardness: a force-push rewind of main passes
description:
Reported by opum-marketplace 2026-09-15 (OMARK-58), routed at opum-agent's direction; confirmed here first-hand rather than taken. lore-cli has LCLI-514, opum-agent has OPAG-152, and opum-agent is taking the source fix to opum-doc's promote-dev-to-main runbook, which is where the shape was copied from into eight repositories.

THE DEFECT. `.github/workflows/promotion-guardrails.yml`, job `main-is-fast-forward-of-dev`, runs inline:

    git merge-base --is-ancestor HEAD origin/dev
    echo "main's new HEAD is a fast-forward of dev."

That proves CONTAINMENT -- main's new HEAD is a commit dev already held. It never reads where main WAS, so it cannot tell a forward promotion from a backwards rewind. A force-push rewinding main to an older commit that is still on dev passes it, and prints the affirmative while commits come off main. opum-marketplace measured it on a scratch repo: genuine promotion GREEN correct, merge commit RED correct, rewind of main from c4 to c1 GREEN and WRONG.

WHY A GREEN HISTORY WAS NEVER EVIDENCE. Both halves of prove-it-rejects and prove-it-accepts pass on the old job and it is still wrong. The gap is between what the verdict CLAIMS -- fast-forwardness -- and what the assertion MEASURES -- containment, which is strictly weaker. The exit code was always right about what it tested. That is why the fix has to put the EMITTED VERDICT under test, not only the exit code, and why extraction to a script is the load-bearing half: inline in a `run:` block the assertion has no tests by construction, which is how this survived in eight repositories.

THE RULESET IS NOT A SECOND LINE OF DEFENCE HERE, and this is the part I had to measure rather than inherit. opum-marketplace's fleet table has quest-cli as `main rules=1 protected=true`, which reads as defense-in-depth. Both halves of that measurement are correct -- I re-ran them -- but the inference does not survive the next call: ruleset 22833771 (`require-ci-on-main`, zero bypass actors) carries exactly ONE rule, `required_status_checks` with contexts source-gates / Tracker integrity / lore check, and NO `non_fast_forward` rule and no `deletion` rule. Required checks gate a push on the pushed COMMIT's own check history, not on which direction the branch moved, and every commit ever promoted to main carries those three contexts by construction -- that is what promotion means here. So a force-push rewinding main to any previously promoted commit is pushing a commit the ruleset is already satisfied by, and it is allowed.

The sharp form: THE RULESET BACKS UP EXACTLY THE HALF OF THE GUARD THAT ALREADY WORKS AND PROVIDES NOTHING FOR THE HALF THAT IS BROKEN. Assertion 1 (a foreign commit, a merge-button commit) is genuinely double-covered, because such a commit has no prior green contexts. Assertion 2 (the rewind) has no second line at all. `protected=true` is true and, for this failure mode, inert.

opum-marketplace then measured the same shape in all five supposedly-protected fleet repos including its own -- identical: `non_fast_forward=NO deletion=NO bypass=0`, rules `required_status_checks` only -- and raised OMARK-58 to High. So the five-protected/five-unprotected split circulating in the fleet is beside the point for this failure mode. They also note their contexts run on pushes to dev too, which widens the accepted rewind targets beyond previously-promoted commits; not separately verified here.

THE FIX IS THREE ASSERTIONS, ADDITIVE, NOT A REPLACEMENT. Swapping forward-movement in for containment trades a known blind spot for a new one while looking like a fix; containment is what catches the merge button. Each assertion gets its own message so a failure names which property broke.
  1 containment       main's new HEAD is a commit dev holds           failure
  2 forward movement  main's previous HEAD is an ancestor of it       failure
  3 completeness      main IS dev's tip, not merely part of it        WARNING
Assertion 3 must stay a warning: dev legitimately advancing between the promotion push and the run gives a non-zero count with nothing wrong. It exists because `git push origin dev:main` off a STALE LOCAL dev (ODOC-193) moves main forward to a commit dev genuinely holds -- both hard assertions green, less delivered than intended.

DO NOT SIMPLIFY AWAY THE FORCED BRANCH. In production a rewind of main is essentially always forced, so FORCED fires first and the REWOUND branch reads like dead code in CI logs. Both earn their place: FORCED defaults false when run by hand, and a rewind via the API or delete-and-recreate need not set it. A future author tidying the dead branch restores the defect.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The assertion lives in a file that can be executed and tested outside Actions, not inline in a run: block -- the workflow calls it and passes github.event.before and github.event.forced as inputs
Forward movement is asserted in ADDITION to containment, not instead of it, and each failure message names which property broke
A force-push rewind of main to an older commit that is still on dev is REJECTED -- the case the old job passed while printing its affirmative
A partial promotion (main moved forward but is behind dev, the ODOC-193 stale-local-dev shape) WARNS and does not fail, and names the commits left behind
The emitted verdict is under test, not only the exit code: the success message states the properties actually measured and never 'fast-forward' as a bare claim
Each clause is proven load-bearing by a mutation matrix -- removing any one assertion turns a named test red -- rather than by a green suite

implementationNotes:
IMPLEMENTED AND LANDED. PR #144 squash-merged into dev as 68b8471; required contexts on head 81455fe all green (source-gates twice -- the correct double fire for a source-touching PR -- Tracker integrity, lore check), plus the full six-platform matrix. bun run check: 520 pass, 0 fail, 4384 expect() calls across 59 files.

THE DEFECT HAD THREE SITES, NOT ONE, and the second and third were found only because the first was fixed. Each sits one step UPSTREAM of the last, so each was unreachable from the fix below it.

  1  previous HEAD missing     reported by opum-marketplace; two causes, one diagnosis
  2  origin/dev missing        found by mutating the refspec away and READING the output
  3  fetch itself fails        found by checking a peer's finding against this code

Site 2 is the one worth generalising: the shallow/full split is a property of EVERY site that reports a missing git object, not of the branch someone happened to name. A fix applied at the site where a defect was reported is the easiest kind to under-apply, and I under-applied it once before noticing.

Site 3 was not a silence hole -- this script already annotated and exited 1 where the bash reference dies at exit 128 with nothing. It was a PARAPHRASE hole: `stdio: "ignore"` discarded git's own `fatal: couldn't find remote ref refs/heads/dev`, the most specific fact available, and the paraphrase blamed main's comparison basis rather than the remote. Fixed by splitting the helper on what a non-zero exit MEANS -- gitOk for questions where non-zero is a legitimate ANSWER (is-ancestor, cat-file -e), gitTry for operations where it is a FAILURE, returning {ok, stderr} and quoting git verbatim. That is a typing distinction and therefore mechanical, which is why it went in the helper rather than into a third round of message edits. The general form: A WRAPPER THAT PARAPHRASES A TOOL'S ERROR OWES THE OPERATOR THE ORIGINAL.

MUTATION MATRIX, each clause removed in turn, each selectively red:
  drop assertion 2 (forward movement)                5
  drop assertion 1 (containment)                     1
  drop the FORCED branch                             1
  assertion 3 fails instead of warns                 1
  unset BEFORE_SHA defaults to zero                  1
  drop the shallow branch                            1
  collapse the previous-HEAD pair to one message     2
  collapse the origin/dev pair to one message        2
  drop the explicit fetch refspec                    1
  revert gitTry to gitOk at the fetch site           1
  replace the workflow's run: line with a comment    1
A blanket revert to the old one-liner reddens all of them, which is the WEAKER result: uniform redness shows only that the suite noticed something.

ONE OF MINE, CAUGHT BY A MUTANT. The full-clone test asserted absence of "fetch-depth: 0'" -- with the trailing quote, lifted from the message it came from -- and a combined-message mutant writing "fetch-depth: 0." walked through the entire suite. An absence assertion has to name the token, not the token as punctuated in the one message it was copied from. Fixed; the mutant now reddens both halves of the pair.

AND ONE IN THE FIXTURE, arrived at independently of opum-marketplace's identical error. I cloned --depth 1 with no --branch, and this scratch remote's default branch is dev, so origin/dev existed for free and the shallow branch was reachable whatever the fetch did -- a fixture that could not fail. Re-cut to --depth 1 --branch main, the production shape. The measurement showing it now discriminates: dropping only the refspec reddens exactly 1; under the old fixture it reddened nothing. opum-cli-e2e's generalisation is the one to keep: a fixture that makes a test pass for a reason the test does not name is indistinguishable from a passing test, so state what the fixture supplies that production might not. Both load-bearing properties of the clone (file:// and --branch main) are now named in a comment beside it with what each would have hidden.

WIRING IS UNPROVEN IN BOTH DIRECTIONS AND THE RECORD SAYS SO. The job fires only on push-to-main, so it reports "skipping" on every PR including the one that added it. The next real promotion buys the ACCEPT direction only, read out of the job log. The REJECT direction would mean deliberately pushing a bad state to main and will not be manufactured. Mutation proves the suite's LOGIC goes red; that a non-zero exit reddens the CI check is WIRING, a separate object (opum-marketplace, after nearly closing its own equivalent on mutation alone). What this does buy toward it is a test asserting the workflow calls the script from a `run:` line rather than a path a comment mentions -- replacing that line with a comment reddens exactly that case.

THE RULESET FINDING, recorded here because it is the reason this matters rather than a detail of it: quest-cli's require-ci-on-main ruleset (22833771, zero bypass actors) carries exactly one rule, required_status_checks, and no non_fast_forward or deletion rule. Required checks gate a push on the pushed COMMIT's check history, not on direction, and every commit ever promoted to main carries all three contexts by construction. So a rewind to a previously promoted commit satisfies the ruleset and is allowed. The ruleset backs up exactly the half of the guard that already works and provides nothing for the half that was broken. Measured against the live API; opum-marketplace then found the identical shape in all five supposedly-protected fleet repos, and opum-web drew the conclusion neither of us had: since no ruleset in the fleet speaks about direction, the tier-3 rail against force-push is not a local control anywhere -- it is the ONLY control against a rewind.

NOT copied from opum-marketplace's assert-main-fast-forward.sh: this is a .mjs because every CI assertion in this repository is one and there is no shell script in the tree. That divergence incidentally avoided the unfixed 2>/dev/null on their fetch, which opum-agent confirmed at 21:40Z is theirs alone among the fleet's implementations.

PROCESS SLIP, recorded rather than tidied away: this task went from created straight to implemented without ever being In Progress. task-execution says claim it first, and the claim is what tells a concurrent session the work is taken. Nothing collided here because no other session touched this repository's tracker tonight, so the cost was zero and the habit is still wrong -- and it only surfaced at completion, because 'To Do -> Done' is an illegal transition (exit 6, validation) and the CLI refused it. The status flow caught what my own discipline did not, which is the better outcome of the two but not a substitute for it. opum-cli-e2e hit the same refusal tonight from the other side and asked about its error envelope; the refusal itself is correct and deliberate.
finalSummary:
promotion-guardrails.yml asserted that main's new HEAD is contained in dev and reported that it was a fast-forward of dev -- containment measured, fast-forwardness claimed. A force-push rewinding main to an older commit still on dev passed while printing the affirmative. Reported by opum-marketplace (OMARK-58), confirmed here, fixed by extracting the assertion to scripts/qualification/promotion-fast-forward.mjs with three additive assertions: containment (kept -- it catches a merge-button commit), forward movement (added -- the half never measured), and completeness as a WARNING (main is dev's tip, not merely part of it; a warning because dev legitimately advancing after the push gives the same count).

The defect turned out to have three sites, each one step upstream of the last and unreachable from the fix below it: the previous-HEAD test, the origin/dev resolution, and the fetch itself. Sites 2 and 3 were found here, by reading a mutant's output rather than its red/green, and by checking a peer's report against this code rather than accepting it. Site 3 was a paraphrase hole, not a silence hole -- git's own error was discarded by stdio: ignore -- and is fixed by typing the helper on whether a non-zero exit is an answer or a failure.

Verified by an 11-mutant matrix in which each clause removed reddens its own named test rather than the suite going uniformly red, plus bun run check at 520 pass / 0 fail across 59 files, and required contexts green on head 81455fe. Two defects of my own were caught in the process and are recorded: an absence assertion coupled to the punctuation of the message it was copied from, and a fixture that could not fail because it supplied origin/dev for free.

CI WIRING IS UNPROVEN IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, deliberately. The job fires only on push-to-main so it skips on every PR; the next real promotion buys the accept direction only, and the reject direction would mean pushing a bad state to main. What is bought is a test that the workflow invokes the script from a run: line rather than a path named in a comment.
